objective: Proof, written before the run: a subdivision keeps k and lambda; fills of triples give a full grid only with one or two middles; from a full grid the rule with no knot-sharing condition refills every new row or column forever.
status: Proved 2026-11-18 (referee pending): a subdivision keeps k and lambda; on a line with fills of triples a full grid needs at most two middles and every allowed fill; the never-nest rule with any old pairs (NNF), given the number two and reading only the states, reaches a full grid from any line before its first subdivision and refills every new row or column forever; the corner rule across crossing splits (CC) refills from a full grid and never fills a line; after the read-out, under CC a split that crosses nothing never comes to cross one.
title: Subdivisions keep the orders; fills of triples; refilling from a full grid
